Author: Anil Verma Bench: Anil Verma

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10148  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT GWALIOR  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ANIL VERMA  ON THE 7 th OF MAY, 2025  CRIMINAL REVISION No. 151 of 2007  LAXMAN  Versus  INDRABHAN AND OTHERS  Appearance:

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT GWALIOR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ms. Akanksha Dhakad - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Pradeep Katare - Advocate for respondents No.1 to   Shri Nirmal Sharma - Public Prosecutor for

respondent N  ORDER Victim/applicant has preferred this criminal revision under Section 397 r/w Section 401 of Cr.P.C.
against the impugned judgment dated 6.11.2006 passed by First Additional Sessions Judge,
Ashoknagar in Criminal Appeal No.45/2006, modified the impugned judgment dated 27.12.2005 passed in Criminal Case No.376/2005 by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Ashoknagar, whereby the respondents have been convicted and sentenced for the offence under Section 324/34 of IPC.

2. Brief facts of the case of the prosecution are that on 22.1.2005 at about 11:00 AM, when the complainant/applicant Laxman was on his way to home from his farm house along with his son Karan Singh, respondents/accused persons met them at Naka and started abusing them and respondent No.4 Ashok gave him axe blow, due to which, complainant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10148 2 CRR-151-2007 Laxman sustained injury over his head and right leg.
When Karan tried to save his father, Mahendra, Gudda and Indrabhan started beating him.
The complainant lodged an FIR at police Station Ashoknagar.
MLC report of the victim was conducted by concerned Doctor and after completion of the investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
3. The Trial Court has framed the charge under Section 324 of IPC against respondent Ashok and Section 324/34 of IPC against rest of the respondents.
They abjured their guilt and pleaded for complete innocence.

After completion of trial, Trial Court has convicted respondent Ashok for the offence under Section 324 of IPC and rest of the accused persons have been convicted for the offence Laxman vs Indrabhan on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69542128/
1 under Section 324/34 of IPC and each of them sentenced six months RI with fine of Rs.500/-, with usual default stipulations.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An appeal has been filed against the said conviction and sentence which has been allowed and, accordingly, respondent Ashok has been convicted for the offence under Section 323 of IPC instead of Section 324 of IPC and sentenced only fine of Rs.1000/- with usual default stipulation.
All other respondents/accused persons were acquitted from the charges under Section 324/34 of IPC.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, the complainant/applicant has preferred this revision petition before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant contended that the impugned judgment passed by the Lower Appellate Court is illegal, arbitrary and against the law.

On the basis of cogent evidence available on record, it has been proved that the complainant has suffered severe injuries over his head and right leg by sharp cutting object axe and respondents/accused Mahendra, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10148 3 CRR-151-2007 Gudda and Indrabhan also participated in the incident in an active manner and they assisted Ashok in causing hurt to the complainant in furtherance of their common intention and concerning Doctor specifically stated that the complainant has sustained injuries, but the first appellate Court has ignored the material evidence available on record.

Hence,
he prays that the order of appellate Court be reversed and set aside and the respondents may be convicted for the offence under Section 324/34 of IPC.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.5/State submits that the Court may pass an appropriate order.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 4 opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection by supporting the order of appellate Court.
7. Both the parties are heard and perused the entire record with due care.

8. The moot question before this Court is whether respondents No.1 to 4 deserves to be convicted for the offence under Section 324/34 of IPC or not?
9.

Victim Laxman (PW-1) categorically stated in his statement that at the time of incident, at about 11:00 AM, when he was returning with Karan Singh to his home, nearby the culvert the accused persons abused him in a filthy language and accused Ashok inflicted injury by means of an axe on his head and also on the right leg.
Other co-accused Mahendra, Gudda and Indrabhan also committed marpeet with him and Karan Singh.
No other person was present on the spot.

10. Karan Singh (PW-2) also supported the statement of his father NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10148 4 CRR-151-2007 Laxman and categorically stated in para 1 of his statement that accused Ashok inflicted injury to his father Laxman by means of an axe, due to which, his father sustained injury over his head and right leg and other co- accused Mahendra,
Gudda and Indrabhan also committed marpeet with him by kicks and fists and thereafter fled away from the spot.

2

11. Mangu (PW-3) stated only that he has not seen any incident but Laxman and Omkar Singh told him that accused persons abused them in filthy language and also committed marpeet with him.
12.
Dr. Natwar Singh (PW-5) who has conducted MLC of both the victim persons has categorically stated that he has examined victim Laxman and Karan on 12.4.2005 and given the MLC report Ex.P/2 and P/3.

Dr. Natwar Singh in his cross-examination admits that ..      
            
13.
It is noteworthy that Investigating Officer did not seize any axe from the possession of respondents/accused during investigation.
Even Head Constable Arvind Singh in his deposition did not state anything regarding seizure of axe.

Alleged axe used in the incident neither seized nor sent for any chemical analysis, therefore, in absence of aforesaid material evidence, injuries sustained by the victim Laxman and Karan Singh by means of axe appears to be doubtful.

14. On the basis of forgoing analysis of the statement of the complainant and the finding given by learned Additional Sessions Judge, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner/complainant has failed to prove that he has sustained injuries by means of axe.
Complainant also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10148 5 CRR-151-2007 failed to point out any illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment which requires any interference by this Court.
Accordingly, there is no ground available on record to interfere in the matter.
Hence, this revision petition is hereby dismissed.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE (alok)
